stem: An operations team notices unusual API calls made with a set of temporary credentials that were never issued to any of their applications, along with a spike in outbound network traffic from one EC2 instance that resembles cryptomining. Which service is purpose-built to surface this kind of finding?

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty, which continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC flow log, and DNS activity for this kind of threat
Amazon Macie, which scans S3 buckets for sensitive data and public exposure
Amazon Cognito, configured to flag suspicious end-user sign-in attempts
AWS WAF, with a rate-based rule added to its web ACL

rationale: Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes AWS CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs using threat-intelligence feeds and machine learning, which is exactly the mix needed to flag a compromised credential being used unexpectedly and cryptomining behavior on an EC2 instance. Amazon Macie is scoped to Amazon S3, where it inventories buckets and finds sensitive data and misconfigurations; it does not analyze account activity or network traffic for credential misuse. Amazon Cognito authenticates the end users of an application and is not a threat-detection service for account-wide API activity. AWS WAF inspects HTTP and HTTPS requests reaching a protected resource such as a load balancer or CloudFront distribution; it does not analyze CloudTrail events or EC2 network traffic for compromised credentials.
